page: Microsoft Azure F8-4amds_v7 is a virtual machine featuring a 4-vCPU dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor based on the x86_64 architecture running at up to 4.5 GHz. The instance provisions 4 physical cores with 1 thread per core, accompanied by 48 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It incorporates vector instruction extensions including AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16. System memory is sized at 64.0 GB of RAM, offering a high allocation of 16.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is provided via an integrated 944 GB NVMe SSD. It contains no dedicated GPU accelerators and provisions zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier single-threaded performance alongside balanced multi-core capabilities. The single-core stress-ng benchmark achieved 3541.48, placing in the top 10%, while multi-core stress-ng reached 14063.2. Compression and decompression tests reflect similar strengths, with single-threaded gzip hitting 38.57 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression achieving 16.95 GB/sec, both scoring in the top 10%. Memory throughput reached 52.32 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 34.33 GB/sec for uncached write operations. Text generation for small 135M language models performed strongly at 331.4 tokens/sec, while medium 7B model prompt processing yielded a weaker 29.74 tokens/sec.

The 1:16 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides significant memory density relative to core count, allowing memory-heavy services to run efficiently without paying for unneeded vCPUs. The included 944 GB NVMe SSD delivers fast local disk IOPS suitable for caching and intermediate storage. Given the 4 dedicated high-frequency cores, high memory ratio, and NVMe disk, the F8-4amds_v7 is well aligned for in-memory caching systems, database operations, compression-heavy ETL pipelines, and memory-intensive web workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure F8-4amds_v7 is an x86_64 virtual machine featuring 4 dedicated physical cores on an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz. Equipped with 64.0 GB of memory (16.0 GB per core) and a bundled 944 GB local NVMe SSD, it delivers high memory density alongside top-tier single-core compute performance. Benchmark evaluation highlights top-10% results in single-core stress-ng (3541.48) and single-threaded gzip compression (38.57 GB/sec), coupled with average multi-threaded scaling and memory bandwidth (52.32 GB/sec uncached read). The system does not include dedicated GPU accelerators. With its large memory capacity relative to compute cores and integrated high-speed local disk, the instance provides cost-efficient operational capability for in-memory databases, caching engines like Redis, single-thread-limited processes, and data compression pipelines.
